applicability: any repository whose tests shell out to a version-control or host tool. A shared hermetic fixture helper would prevent the class and is deliberately unbuilt: one consumer today, so it waits trigger-bound like any other mechanism

evidence.source_reference: PR #130 and PR #131 automated review findings; two occurrences in one pull request

expected_behavior: A fixture that runs a real external command pins every host setting that decides what the command prints, in the fixture's own local configuration, before asserting on its output. Reproduce the hostile setting and record the before and after results rather than reasoning that the default is safe.
observation: A test fixture that shells out to a real version-control status command inherits the invoking developer's global configuration, and two host settings silently decided its verdict. A global excludes-file entry covering the file under test would make a non-vacuity proof pass whether or not the repository rule existed, a false green. A global setting suppressing untracked-file display failed three cases on that machine alone, a false red, reproduced by pointing the tool at a synthetic global config: three failures before pinning the setting locally, none after.
reason: Two verified occurrences in one pull request: a global excludes entry made a non-vacuity proof green independent of the repository rule, and a global setting hiding untracked files produced three machine-local failures. The site fix landed in the fleet-doctor test, which now pins both host settings locally and records the reproduction. The transferable rule has no owner: a fixture that shells out to a real external command pins every host setting that decides that command's output, and the proof is reproducing the hostile setting rather than assuming the default is safe.
